title: The Big Five personality model
summary: The five basic dimensions, what each measures, and how to apply them to people at work.

chunks.heading: What the Big Five is
chunks.explanation_md:
The **Big Five** is a personality assessment model with **five basic dimensions**. The slide credits it as the **John Bearden tool**.

These five dimensions **underlie all others** and cover most of the significant variation in human personality. Test scores on these traits do a **very good job of predicting how people behave in real-life situations**.

The five traits: **Extroversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Emotional Stability, Openness to experience**. A handy memory trick is to remember the first letters, but only the names matter in the exam.

chunks.heading: Each of the five dimensions
chunks.explanation_md:
- **Extroversion**: sociable, expressive, self-assured and confident.
- **Agreeableness**: good-natured, cooperative and trusting.
- **Conscientiousness** (a measure of **reliability**): responsible, dependable, determined and organized.
- **Emotional Stability** (the **ability to handle stress**): calm, self-confident and secure on the positive side; nervous, depressed and insecure on the negative side.
- **Openness to Experience**: imaginative, creative, curious, artistic, sensitive and intellectual, versus conventional and conservative people who find comfort in the familiar.

To apply it to a work situation: ask which dimension explains the behavior. A person who stays calm under pressure is high on emotional stability; one who is dependable and organized is high on conscientiousness; one who is cooperative and trusting is high on agreeableness.

questions.stem: List the Big Five personality traits and give a one-line description of each.
questions.model_answer_md:
The **Big Five** are five basic dimensions that underlie all others:
- **Extroversion**: sociable, expressive, self-assured and confident.
- **Agreeableness**: good-natured, cooperative and trusting.
- **Conscientiousness**: responsible, dependable, determined, organized (reliability).
- **Emotional Stability**: calm, self-confident, secure versus nervous, depressed, insecure (handling stress).
- **Openness to Experience**: imaginative, creative, curious, artistic versus conventional.

questions.stem: Explain conscientiousness and emotional stability with a workplace example for each.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Conscientiousness** is a measure of reliability: responsible, dependable, determined and organized. Example: an employee who meets every deadline and keeps work organized.

**Emotional Stability** is the ability to handle stress: calm, self-confident and secure on the positive side, nervous, depressed and insecure on the negative side. Example: a manager who stays calm under pressure, versus one who becomes nervous and insecure.

Both help predict behavior at work.

rubric.point: Emotional stability defined as handling stress

questions.stem: Differentiate between the Big Five model and the MBTI.
questions.model_answer_md:
The **MBTI** classifies people on four pairs (E/I, S/N, T/F, J/P) from a 100-question test into 16 types, and its results tend to be unrelated to job performance.

The **Big Five** uses five basic dimensions (Extroversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Emotional Stability, Openness) that underlie all others, and its scores predict behavior in many real-life situations.

In short, MBTI sorts people into types; the Big Five describes five dimensions and predicts behavior better.

rubric.point: Big Five predicts behavior in real-life situations

questions.stem: Apply the Big Five Personality Model to an organizational situation, showing how the traits influence employee behaviour and performance.
questions.model_answer_md:
The **Big Five** has five basic dimensions that underlie all others, and test scores predict how people behave in real-life situations, so it is useful for understanding employees.

Consider a team in an organization:
- **Extroversion**: a sociable, expressive and confident member leads discussions and handles clients.
- **Agreeableness**: a good-natured, cooperative and trusting member builds team harmony.
- **Conscientiousness**: a responsible, dependable and organized member delivers reliably; this is the measure of reliability.
- **Emotional Stability**: a calm, secure member keeps performing under stress, while a nervous or insecure member struggles when pressure rises.
- **Openness to Experience**: an imaginative, curious member generates new ideas, while a conventional member prefers the familiar.

A manager can use this to place people in roles that fit, for example a calm and dependable person for high-pressure work. This supports personality-job fit, which leads to excellence and job satisfaction.

Conclusion: the Big Five helps explain and predict behavior and performance.

rubric.point: Links to behavior and performance, personality-job fit

questions.stem: Explain the Big Five model fully and discuss how a manager could use it to build a team.
questions.model_answer_md:
The **Big Five** is a personality assessment model with five basic dimensions that underlie all others and cover most significant variation in human personality. Scores predict behavior in many real-life situations.

**The five traits**: Extroversion (sociable, expressive, self-assured), Agreeableness (good-natured, cooperative, trusting), Conscientiousness (responsible, dependable, determined, organized; reliability), Emotional Stability (calm, self-confident, secure; ability to handle stress) and Openness to Experience (imaginative, creative, curious, artistic versus conventional).

**Team building**: a manager can look for a mix. Extroverts help with communication, agreeable people with cooperation, conscientious people with reliable delivery, emotionally stable people for stressful tasks and open people for creative work. Matching traits to job needs gives personality-job fit, which leads to excellence and job satisfaction.

Conclusion: because the dimensions predict behavior, the Big Five is a practical guide for placing people and managing teams.
